title: Dense-open isomorphism for a fixed saturated logarithmic blowup tower
statement: Let $T$ be a finite saturated logarithmic blowup tower [def-trf-fs-log-blowup] and let $p_i:X_i\to X_0$ be log morphisms with $p_0$ the identity [def-per-log-morphism-identity] and $p_{i+1}=p_i\circ b_i$ [def-per-log-morphism-composition]. Suppose only that the initial and terminal fs log schemes $X_0$ and $X_N$ are log regular [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]. Then there exist dense open subschemes $U\subseteq X_N$ and $W\subseteq X_0$ [def-weil-open-immersion] and an isomorphism $e:U\simeq W$ such that $p_N\circ j_U=j_W\circ e$. No projectivity, terminal freeness, quasi-compactness or integralness is assumed. Length-zero towers and empty endpoints are allowed.

source.place: VI 1.2, 1.6--1.7, pp.69--70; VIII 3.3.8--3.3.11, pp.107--108, and 3.4.8, p.111. Original parent steps 9--10, omitting the separate integrality conclusion.

proof.text: For either endpoint $Z$ of the fixed tower, let $U_Z$ be the zero-characteristic locus. It is open: on an fs chart it is the intersection of the finitely many unit loci of monoid generators, hence a principal open on each affine chart; these opens give the locus etale locally and descend to an open by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-lfp-open]. Every irreducible component has a generic point by [lem-sc-scheme-sober]. Its ordinary local ring has dimension zero, since primes in that localization correspond to primes contained in a minimal prime. Its strict local ring also has dimension zero by [lem-sc-strict-henselization-dimension]. The log-regular dimension equality then forces the rank of the sharp characteristic group to be zero. That group is finitely generated and torsion free by the saturation and sharpness argument in step 2; [lem-trf-fg-torsionfree-group-free] implies it is zero, and the characteristic monoid embeds in it, so is zero. Thus $U_Z$ contains every generic point and is dense.

source.place: VI 1.2 and 1.6--1.7; dense triviality locus, proved here from the log-regular dimension condition at generic points.

proof.text: For one stage the saturated chart group is generated by $P$ and differences of its elements. At a source point all its chart monomials are units if all those from $P$ are units: the differences are ratios of units, and saturation adjoins elements a positive power of whose image is a unit, hence whose image is a unit. Conversely, if all source chart monomials are units, so are the images of $P$; the local map on ordinary local rings reflects units, so the image point has zero characteristic. The chart description [lem-trf-coherent-log-ideal-chart-construction] therefore gives $U_{X_{i+1}}=b_i^{-1}(U_{X_i})$. Over $U_{X_i}$ every nonempty log ideal is the whole unit monoid, already invertible, so its saturated log blowup is the identity by the universal property in [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]. Iterating gives $U_Y=b^{-1}(U_V)\simeq U_V$. Both opens are dense by the preceding step, so $b$ is birational. The equations on p identify its terminal map with the restricted composite, so the inclusions commute with this isomorphism. This also covers the identity tower and empty endpoints.

source.place: VIII 3.3.8--3.3.11 and 3.4.8; the dense-open and integrality conclusions from the explicit blowup charts.

theorem saturatedLogTower_denseOpen
    (T : SaturatedLogBlowupTower.{u})
    (p : ∀ i : Fin (T.length + 1), EtaleLogHom (T.level i) (T.level 0))
    (hp0 : p 0 = EtaleLogHom.id (T.level 0))
    (hp : ∀ i : Fin T.length, (T.arrow i).CompEq (p i.castSucc) (p i.succ))
    (hstart : (T.level 0).IsLogRegular)
    (hfinish : (T.level (Fin.last T.length)).IsLogRegular) :
    ∃ (U : (T.level (Fin.last T.length)).scheme.Opens)
      (W : (T.level 0).scheme.Opens) (e : U.toScheme ≅ W.toScheme),
      Dense (U : Set (T.level (Fin.last T.length)).scheme) ∧
      Dense (W : Set (T.level 0).scheme) ∧
      U.ι ≫ (p (Fin.last T.length)).base = e.hom ≫ W.ι
